### Observed differences

- Activity A02 appeared in fewer traces in the later window: about 15 in 100 traces (30 of 200) contained it, compared with about 27 in 100 traces (53 of 200) in the earlier window. [OCC001]
- The mean number of A02 executions per trace fell from about 0.30 to about 0.16, a drop of roughly 0.14 occurrences per trace. [OCC001]
- Repetition of A02 within a trace was rare in both windows (recurrence support about 0.03 earlier versus 0.01 later), so the difference lies mainly in how often traces included A02 at all, not in repeated execution. [OCC001]
- This difference is unusual for a random re-split of the pooled traces: it exceeds about 995 of 1,000 reference comparisons. [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a structural change in the process. Only one evidence item qualified across 87 tested units, whereas about 0.43 items would be expected by chance in an unchanged process; a single item is what a stable process typically produces, even one whose difference looks large against random re-splits. The apparent drop in A02 participation could therefore reflect sampling variation between the two windows rather than a real change in how often A02 is executed.
